items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: He said, “Well I want to sign you guys for a couple of records.” So he did and those paid, the first one paid $13,500 and the second was $15,000. So I negotiated that.

ctx.x: Well we had them but we had been dropped by RCA. We did not have a record deal. I had the tapes and somehow word got around about them and these two small labels, one was in Baltimore, one was in Washington. They called me and they wanted to do a thing with two albums, that I had enough material for two LPs. So they split it up. One took one and the other took the other. They are, “Phil Woods’ Quartet Live” and “More Live”

they were called. They were the first records that I got production credit on. And you know we went from making — you know I was able to negotiate you know a fairly nice budget for those. They were already recorded and I hadn’t spent a lot of money recording them so I was able to get probably a total of maybe 15 grand for both of them and then the next thing that happened was Ron Goldstein from Island Records called me because I had met him when he was with Warner Brothers Records. And he was starting out as…
